ideas.title: Climb aboard and sail it: the yacht in Jump in
ideas.critique: Here the still yacht from the last post gets something it never had: a player at the controls, with a live 3D flow solve feeding force back into a rolling body, and the island has never let the player steer a simulated vehicle. It only works if the stall and the moving trim point really come out of the solver as you play; a lift curve read from a table would make it one more cart on rails.

ideas.title: The kite that switches off
ideas.critique: A real low-Re stall you fly at the edge of is a good dexterity toy, and it is flown by hand, not left alone in front of a fixed camera. But a solved cloth shape on a string over the sand is close kin to the darts and the sail, and it barely moves the cart forward.

ideas.title: Plates that fizz: Planté's lead accumulator
same_form: A top over a ring of lodestone
ideas.critique: This is one more electrochemical jar on the bench, filmed close while it changes, which is exactly the recipe of the last ten posts. Storage is a real part of the big goal, and the forming ritual is the only new thing in it, but bubbles plus a colour change worked out from Faraday's law will read as the clay pots again.

ideas.title: Hike out or go over
ideas.critique: Friends as ballast who don't always listen is a real creature-and-player interaction the island lacks, and a wheel lifting in a gust is easy to share. It can't exist until the yacht sails, and three fixed seat positions would turn the rigid body into a switch.

ideas.title: The windmill that lights the hut
ideas.critique: The glowing filament has been posted before, and a dusk film of a rotor turning is the same device-watched-alone shape again. It is a core road step, and the hut lit by the gusts is a nice image, but facing and pitch are thin as play unless the wind really shifts under you.

ideas.title: Tug of war with my motor
ideas.critique: This is funny, and it is the first time the friends test a machine, which is the kind of creature contest the human asks for. But the friends' pull will most likely be a number typed in with a sliding animation, and once you have seen who wins the setups run out.

ideas.title: Wet sand, dry sand
ideas.critique: A beach whose ground really changes with the tide is a new layer of the world, and timing the cart with it is a good daily rhythm. But traced stills of a darker band are only a look until something drives over it, and hand-picked moisture-to-Bekker numbers stay a one-setup rig.

ideas.title: A message in a bottle for the human
ideas.critique: Floating with wind and wave drift has been done with the logs, and the bottle adds little physics beyond them; a note to the human is a sweet premise but also a predictable one. Finding a bottle days later is the only lasting hook, and it has nothing to do with the cart.

ideas.title: Sand fence ramp, in play
ideas.nearest: Dandelion clocks, a take that misses
ideas.critique: Shaping land with solved wind and saltation is real terrain physics the player authors, and the island hasn't had that. A time-lapse of drifts is slow to watch, though, and it only pays off if the drift really depends on where the fences stand.

ideas.title: Lumi's sulk walk
ideas.critique: Lumi's moods on its body are a standing goal of the human's, and a sulk is a gait one could predict from it, so this carries out an example the goals name. Kicked sand and deeper prints help, but it is still mostly an animation swap tied to a mood flag.
